title: The original completion augmentation and the selected reduction calculus
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and W a scheme on which l is invertible in all residue fields. The actual integral completion functor is naturally isomorphic to the selected coherent reduction followed by total derived limit, and its original augmentation followed by this isomorphism equals the actual unit of the selected reduction/limit adjunction, on every ambient derived object. No completeness or boundedness is assumed. [def-pod-completion-reindex-models]

source.place: Steps 1 and 5; strict quotient and Roos comparison argument.

proof.text:
take the normalized primitive completion model on the singleton family W.
Both its reduction functor and the selected reduction functor are left adjoint to
the same total-limit functor. The unique left-adjoint comparison identifies their
actual units. Whisker that comparison by total limit and compose it with the
primitive model's completion comparison. The primitive unit normalization and the
unit formula for the unique left-adjoint comparison give the required equality.
The construction does not use nonemptiness of W or boundedness of a complex.

lean.statement:
theorem podReindexingCompletionNormalization (W : Scheme.{t})
    [∀ w : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField w)] :
    ∃ e : IntegralOnSlice.completion l E W none ≅
        (podReindexCalculus l E W).reduction ⋙ coefficientSequenceLimit l E W,
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E W),
        (IntegralOnSlice.completionUnit l E W none).app K ≫ e.hom.app K =
          (podReindexCalculus l E W).adjunction.unit.app K
